title: First run does what install-agent.sh does: config, start at login, tailscale serve

history.what: review: no drift, failure paths, existing installs

before.done_when: with no config.json, Tether reads the signed-in login from tailscale status, writes config.json, installs the same LaunchAgent and runs tailscale serve; SelfTest checks the config and plist text match install-agent.sh's

done_when: with no config.json, Tether reads the signed-in login from tailscale status, writes config.json, installs the same LaunchAgent and runs tailscale serve; with an existing config.json it keeps it and clears updateFrom; SelfTest compares against install-agent.sh itself and covers the four failure paths and the existing-config case
body: Drift: SelfTest reads scripts/lib/install-agent.sh from the repo and compares the config.json keys and LaunchAgent plist it would write with the Swift output, so a change to one fails the test until the other matches. Failure paths, each a Setup Assistant message, never swallowed: tailscale not installed, not signed in, HTTPS certificates off, tailscale serve failing (its stderr shown). Existing installs (Jordan's three Macs): a release app finding a config.json keeps it and the LaunchAgent, rewrites only the app path, clears updateFrom so UpdateMode picks the release route, and leaves the source checkout alone for the developer route (D-3).
